name: Community — MiniMax H3 (Turbo, Fully Accelerated)
author: larryvrh + kijai + xmarre
description: MiniMax H3 text-to-video with every acceleration technique stacked: MiniMax H3 Turbo LoRA (v4-600 EMA, applied via the dedicated ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo loader - required on our pruned int8 base, since a generic LoRA loader silently drops the adaln timing-curve weights) + MiniMax H3 Turbo Sampler (dual-schedule aware, auto-detects native ModelSamplingAV) + SageAttention (KJNodes) + MiniMax H3 Sigma Shift (native noise-schedule control) + Spectrum (xmarre's spectral-feature-forecasting accelerator, ~30-40% fewer transformer evaluations) + Sol-Attn (sparse attention, reduced VRAM). Stack order and recommended settings sourced from the community workflow this pack is based on. Steps reduced from the official 20 down to 10 (can go as low as 4 per the source video, at a quality cost). Tested T2V at 5s/480p/10 steps: 84.1s on engine v0.31.0 (was 99.1s on v0.30.1), LoRA log-confirmed fully applied (208/208 backbone modules + 51 adaln modules, zero dropped keys) - clean video output across sampled frames, no artifacts, no visible plastic-skin/over-sharp-grain look. That is 2.03x the official 20-step MiniMax H3 preset measured the same way, making this the first preset here to pass 2x. Research/experimental preset - Spectrum is an approximate accelerator (not bit-identical output). IMPORTANT, from Spectrum's own maintainer as of 2026-08-13: few-step acceleration LoRAs - explicitly including Turbo - are NOT recommended alongside Spectrum for quality-critical work. Reported degradation covers composition, action and motion, reduced natural detail, and a smooth/plasticky look. He also found the same degradation running the acceleration LoRA WITHOUT Spectrum, so this is the Turbo LoRA's character rather than a Spectrum interaction - but it means this pack stacks two things whose author does not recommend combining them. Use it for speed; use the Sol-Attn + EasyCache pack at 20 steps when fidelity matters. Settings here are blend_weight 0.50, audio_blend_weight 0.00, offline_smoothing_replay on. Note audio_blend_weight 0 does NOT make a forecast step equivalent to a real transformer evaluation - it only stops direct spectral blending of audio rows; Spectrum still substitutes predicted hidden features on forecast steps. At 10 steps this preset runs roughly 5 real evaluations and 5 forecasts, which is the short-trajectory regime the maintainer flags as having few actual anchors. Pinned against Spectrum v0.2.5; v0.2.6 and v0.2.7 since added native ER-SDE support and model-aware forecasting, which this workflow does not yet configure.

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Text to Video (Turbo, Fully Accelerated)
presets.description: Describe a scene and get video with matching stereo sound. Stacks Turbo LoRA + SageAttention + Sigma Shift + Spectrum + Sol-Attn for the fastest MiniMax H3 preset in this repo. Research/experimental - Spectrum's forecasted steps change the denoising trajectory, so output isn't bit-identical to unaccelerated MiniMax H3. Needs four custom nodes. Do not also pick this LoRA in the user LoRA slot - the preset applies minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors itself, and selecting it again stacks it to double strength (over-sharp grain and artifacts). SimpliGen 1.46.0 began listing every LoRA found on disk, so it now appears in the picker even though it is an internal pack dependency.

extensions.name: ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo
extensions.description: Turbo LoRA loader node + dual-schedule sampler node (required - the workflow will fail to load without it)

extensions.name: ComfyUI-KJNodes
extensions.description: Provides PathchSageAttentionKJ - this workflow applies SageAttention itself, via this node. IMPORTANT: do not stack a second model-level SageAttention patch on top of it. If your setup applies SageAttention globally (ComfyUI's --use-sage-attention, or a host app that patches the model for you), the two patches together can make Turbo output numerically invalid - reported as black or garbage frames. On SimpliGen this is handled automatically: the app withholds its own per-preset patch for this preset, so this node is the only one active.

extensions.name: ComfyUI-Spectrum-MiniMax-H3
extensions.description: Spectral-feature-forecasting accelerator for native MiniMax H3 (SpectrumApplyMiniMaxH3 node). NOT pre-installed by SimpliGen.

extensions.name: ComfyUI-SolAttn_triton
extensions.description: Sol-Attn sparse-attention node (Triton kernels). NOT pre-installed by SimpliGen. Requires the engine's Python to have dev headers (Python.h / python3XX.lib) for Triton's JIT compiler - present from SimpliGen 1.43.x onward. REQUIRES SimpliGen Settings > Advanced > 'Faster Attention' to be ON - that toggle controls whether the triton-windows pip package stays installed, and without it this node fails to import ('No module named triton'). SimpliGen's own 'Repair now' prompt will NOT fix this, and that still holds on SimpliGen 1.46.0, which added detection and repair of half-installed custom nodes: that targets incomplete installs, and this node is complete - it ships no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or install script, so there is no declared dependency for a repair to reinstall. Only re-enabling Faster Attention restores triton. Note that toggle does two distinct things: globally it installs/removes the triton + sageattention packages (needed here), while per-preset it decides whether SimpliGen applies its own SageAttention patch (withheld for this preset, which is what we want - see the KJNodes note on double-patching). Leaving it ON is correct for this preset: the packages stay installed and SimpliGen still withholds the duplicate patch.

requirements.notes: Same base weights as SimpliGen's official MiniMax H3 pack (pruned int8 + nvfp4 encoder) plus the ~744MB Turbo LoRA - no new downloads beyond that. Needs FOUR custom nodes: ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo (LoRA loader + dual-schedule sampler - required on this pruned base, a generic LoRA loader silently drops the adaln timing-curve weights), ComfyUI-KJNodes, ComfyUI-Spectrum-MiniMax-H3, and ComfyUI-SolAttn_triton (Sol-Attn also needs SimpliGen 1.43.x+ and Faster Attention enabled - see the extension note). Directly measured by this repo's maintainer: 5s/480p/10 steps in 84.1s on engine v0.31.0 (99.1s when first measured on v0.30.1), with the LoRA log-confirmed fully applied (zero dropped keys). Recommend 10 steps for quality; can go as low as 4 for speed per the source video, at a real quality cost. RAM requirement verified downward: every preset in this pack has been run repeatedly on a 32GB machine (31.2GB usable) with a 12GB RTX 4070 Ti, so the earlier 48GB figure was too conservative. The engine streams model weights rather than holding them resident, which is what makes a ~20GB checkpoint workable well under its own size. 16GB has not been tested.

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Reference to Video (Turbo, Fully Accelerated)
presets.description: Supply reference images or sound to steer the cast, style, and audio of a generated shot. Stacks Turbo LoRA + SageAttention + Sigma Shift + Spectrum + Sol-Attn. Measured at 5s/480p/10 steps across separate runs at 93-116s, in the same range as this pack's T2V preset rather than markedly slower - unlike the unaccelerated Turbo and Sol-Attn packs, where reference conditioning costs noticeably more than plain text. Those R2V figures were taken on engine v0.30.1 and have not been re-measured since v0.31.0, which took 8-18% off every T2V preset; expect them to be pessimistic. Reference conditioning also varies far more run to run than T2V does, so treat the range as a range. Research/experimental - Spectrum forecasted steps change the denoising trajectory, so output is not bit-identical to unaccelerated MiniMax H3. Needs four custom nodes. KNOWN ISSUE - reference VIDEO currently fails on every Turbo-LoRA preset: a reference clip triggers a second conditioning pass at the same timestep, and the ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo node's adaln re-injection crashes on it with 'The size of tensor a (3) must match the size of tensor b (2)'. Reference images and reference audio are unaffected - remove the video and the generation completes. For reference-video work use the Community MiniMax H3 (Sol-Attn + EasyCache) R2V preset, which applies no Turbo LoRA. Upstream node bug, not a pack defect. Do not also pick this LoRA in the user LoRA slot - the preset applies minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors itself, and selecting it again stacks it to double strength (over-sharp grain and artifacts). SimpliGen 1.46.0 began listing every LoRA found on disk, so it now appears in the picker even though it is an internal pack dependency.
presets.tagline: Reference images/video steer the cast and style - fully accelerated
